Subject: Traffic-profile-driven sizing & canary rehearsal for Dedicated migration (BlueHarvest)

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. To make the hosted -> Dedicated sizing deterministic on our side, could you send a representative week of production traffic (token/time series or per-endpoint QPS) and a target RPS/latency SLO you expect for go-live?

What we'll do after receiving that:
- Run a traffic-profile simulation against our pool sizing simulator (multi-seq lengths + KV cache model).
- Produce a proposed GPU mix (A100/RTX/whatever) and an autoscaling curve to meet the requested SLO with margin.
- Schedule a 2-hour canary rehearsal window where we run a mirrored subset of your traffic (read-only) against a Dedicated staging fleet to validate tail latency and cache hit behavior.

I attached a mutual action plan stub and a small sample CSV template for the traffic export. If you prefer, Karthik can host a short collection call to walk through what to export.

Proposed tentative window for the canary rehearsal: Wed 2027-09-29 15:00-17:00 PT (we'll coordinate calendar once you've confirmed).

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

Jonas —

Thanks, that sounds like the right approach. I've attached a redacted 7-day token-level export for our primary inference endpoint and a short README on how the traffic is split across versions. Key asks from our side:

- Target p95 latency <= 450ms for text-generation at our 1k concurrent request baseline.
- We will commit to the initial monthly reserved capacity if the acceptance run meets p95 and no regressions in hallucination rate.

A couple of constraints to flag up front: we cannot accept any production writes during the rehearsal window and we will need an SLA exception on retention for debug logs (internal procurement will follow up).

Sending the files: traffic_profile_export_20270918.csv (redacted).

—Elena

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-09-21T11:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Traffic-profile-driven sizing & canary rehearsal for Dedicated migration (BlueHarvest)

Elena —

Received the CSV, thanks. I ran an initial pass through our simulator and want to call out a few observations before we lock sizing: 

1) Burstiness: I see sustained short bursts (20–30s) that drive queue depth on our current default batching. We'll model a reduced batch timeout for the canary to ensure tail latency stays below 450ms.

2) Sequence length distribution: ~12% of requests exceed 2k tokens and dominate GPU memory usage. For the staging canary we recommend enabling KV-prefetching and a 1.25x memory buffer on the GPU type we propose.

3) Cache hit assumptions: your traffic shows a high degree of prefix reuse (good). Turning on prefix KV caching in Dedicated should reduce effective cost by ~18% and improve median latency. We'll include cache warmup steps in the rehearsal playbook.

Proposed Dedicated staging fleet: 4 nodes (A100-40GB equiv), Nginx fronting for graceful drain, autoscale headroom for 20% traffic surge during the rehearsal. We'll convert that recommendation into a formal sizing doc for Marissa.

Canary data collection plan (short):
- Mirror 10% of production read requests for 2 hours.
- Collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU util, KV-cache hit rate, and token-level error traces.
- Post-run: side-by-side quantized-compared outputs to check quality drift.

If that sounds good I can push the rehearsal playbook by EOD.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Elena —

Appreciate the export and the constraints note. Quick commercial/ops alignment on our side:

- Pricing: Based on Karthik's proposed staging fleet, preliminary reserved-cost estimate is attached. We'll treat the rehearsal as a zero-bill validation run; production billing begins after acceptance.
- MAP: I updated the mutual action plan with deadlines and owners (see attached MAP_BlueHarvest_20270919.pdf).
- Acceptance gates: p95 <= 450ms, no increase in hallucination rate >1.5x baseline, and successful log retention exception workflow signed by procurement.

Could procurement loop in their contract owner and confirm the retention exception timeline? Once procurement signs off we can lock the rehearsal window.

Proposed rehearsal window (tentative): Thu 2027-09-30 16:00-18:00 PT — same as Jonas' earlier ask but shifted to avoid their scheduled nightly jobs.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

2) Liability: Can Redwood confirm there will be no write-paths or data ingestion changes during the canary (read-only mirror)? We need that in writing for our audit trail.

I've attached the SLA_exception_request_20270923.docx with procurement comments. Please respond with the redaction plan and a written confirmation of read-only rehearsal.

Regards,

Hi BlueHarvest procurement / team —

Short answers to the procurement checklist: 

1) Redaction controls: We will stream debug logs to a secure work bucket with an automated PII redaction step (drop SSNs, emails, user identifiers) prior to any human access. The redaction tooling is documented here: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/blueharvest-migration (we'll add the full runbook to the MAP).

2) Write-path confirmation: This rehearsal will be strictly read-only mirror traffic. We will configure the gateway to strip any write-intent headers and block all POSTs to your production write endpoints. Redwood confirms in writing: no production writes or customer data mutation during the rehearsal window.

Operational next steps (we will action once procurement confirms):
- Finalize rehearsal runbook (Karthik to publish).
- Attach HubSpot checklist and invite calendar events (Marissa/Jonas).
- DocuSign: we'll send the SLA exception once the redaction sentence is accepted.

I'll follow up with the rehearsal runbook this afternoon.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
